newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Somali factions demand compensation from U.N..
newsitem.headline: Somali factions demand compensation from U.N..

text.p: Somali faction leaders demanded on Friday the United Nations pay compensation and apologize for atrocities committed in Somalia by U.N. troops between 1992 and 1994.

Twenty-six leaders appealed to U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan to establish a fact-finding mission under the Security Council to determine the "depth and scope" of abuses of authority and mandate by U.N. troops.

"U.N. troops which went to Somalia...indulged in acts of violence and human degredation such as killing, rape, torture, humiliation and imprisonments," the leaders said in a statement issued in Addis Ababa. They did not specify the amount of compensation demanded.
Revelations by Canada, Belgium and Italy, which contributed troops to the U.N. mission, were the tip of the iceberg, the statement said.

A Belgian military court acquitted two ex-paratroopers last week for insufficient evidence after they were accused of threatening behaviour and physical violence towards a Somali boy during their mission in 1993.
The two were charged after a newspaper published a photograph that appeared to show them swinging a Somali boy over a fire.

Thousands of troops served with Operation Restore Hope the U.N. military mission in Somalia set up to ensure the distribution of food aid. Somalia has been without central government since dicator Siad Barre was ousted in 1991.
